description: An additive oscillator: sixteen harmonics drawn as rotating vectors, each with its own magnitude, phase and frequency trim, summed into one wave

params.text: Sets how far the voltage at that harmonic's magnitude CV jack moves its magnitude
Sets how far the voltage at that harmonic's trim CV jack moves its frequency trim
Sets the depth of linear frequency modulation from the LIN FM jack
Sets the depth of exponential frequency modulation from the EXP FM jack
Raises the low harmonics against the high ones at one end of its travel, and the high against the low at the other
An attenuverter setting how far the voltage at the TILT CV jack moves the tilt
Moves the magnitude of every harmonic up or down together
An attenuverter setting how far the voltage at the OFFSET CV jack moves the offset
Stores the screen as a new keyframe, reached over the time set as NEXT KF TIME
Deletes every keyframe stored in the animator
Deletes the keyframe shown as the current one, and the values stored in it
Runs the animation through the stored keyframes, and stops it while it is running
Pauses the animation where it stands, and carries on from there when pressed again
Sets a running animation back to its starting condition
Runs the animation over and over rather than stopping at the last keyframe
Sets the level of the summed output
Sets how much of the voltage at the octave CV jack reaches the octave

inputs.text: Sets the base frequency, 1V per octave
A voltage moving that harmonic's magnitude, scaled by that harmonic's magnitude attenuator
A voltage moving that harmonic's phase
A voltage moving that harmonic's frequency trim; with Frequency Trimmers as FM inputs switched on in the menu it modulates that harmonic's frequency instead
A voltage shifting the octave, scaled by the OCTAVE knob
A signal modulating the base frequency linearly, scaled by LIN FM
A signal modulating the base frequency exponentially, scaled by EXP FM
A voltage moving the tilt, scaled by the TILT CV attenuverter
A voltage moving the offset, scaled by the OFFSET CV attenuverter
A trigger stores the screen as a new keyframe
A trigger runs the animation, and stops it while it is running
A trigger pauses the animation, and carries on from there
A trigger sets a running animation back to its starting condition

outputs.text: The sum of all sixteen harmonics
The sum of the even numbered harmonics
The sum of the odd numbered harmonics
That harmonic on its own, at its own frequency, magnitude and phase
That harmonic on its own at a low frequency, for use as a modulation source; it carries 0V while Low Power Mode is on

notes: each harmonic's magnitude is dragged on its bar, from -2 to +2, with the red line marking 1.0
each harmonic's phase is dragged on its dial, from 0 to 360 degrees
each harmonic's frequency trim is dragged on its dial and moves that harmonic away from exact harmonicity by -20% to +20%; right clicking it resets it to zero
the sign row marks each harmonic as plus or minus, and right clicking it inverts that harmonic's frequency, which this oscillator can run negative
BASE FREQ Hz sets the frequency the harmonics are built on and is dragged on its display; the octave beside it runs from -5 to +5
the animator's displays read the number of stored keyframes, the length of the whole animation in seconds, and which keyframe is being shown
CURR KF TIME is the time taken to reach the keyframe being shown, and NEXT KF TIME the time that will be given to the next one stored
CURR KF TIME and NEXT KF TIME are set by clicking and dragging on them, with a minimum of 0.01 seconds
menu: Set Harmonics ratio to standard tuning — works the sixteen frequencies out from the base frequency as the harmonic series
Set Harmonics ratio to square of position — with to cube of position, to square root of position and to Hammond B3 wheels, the other ways the sixteen frequencies are worked out
Low Power Mode — stops the low frequency copies of the harmonics, which then carry 0V, and saves what they cost to compute
Frequency Trimmers as FM inputs — turns each harmonic's trim CV jack into a linear FM input for that harmonic
Full Reset — returns every harmonic to the module's starting magnitude, phase, trim and sign
Reset to SAW — sets the sixteen magnitudes and phases to build a saw, with Reset to SQUARE and Reset to TRIANGLE beside it
Show Phasor — draws the rotating vectors, with Show Path drawing the path they trace and Show Wave the wave they make
Zoom IN — scales the drawing up, with Zoom OUT and Zoom Reset beside it
Randomize All Magnitudes — scatters the magnitudes across all sixteen harmonics, with Randomize All Phases, Randomize All Frequency Trimmers and Randomize All Frequency Sign beside it
Zero All Magnitudes — clears the magnitudes on all sixteen harmonics, with Zero All Phases, Zero All Frequency Trimmers and Reset All Frequency Sign beside it
Add 1 Random KF, Add 10 Random KFs and Add 100 Random KFs — build an animation of that many random keyframes, taking their range from the magnitudes of the first two harmonics
Load Current Frame To Screen — puts the values of the current keyframe onto the screen, and Save Screen To Current Frame writes what is on the screen back into it
Max AMP Harmonic — sets that harmonic's magnitude to full, with Half AMP Harmonic and Zero AMP Harmonic beside it, on the menu that harmonic's own column carries
Invert Frequency Sign — turns one harmonic's frequency negative, on the menu that harmonic's own column carries; the harmonic's number is printed after the name
0 Phase Harmonic, 90 Phase Harmonic, 180 Phase Harmonic and 270 Phase Harmonic — set one harmonic's phase to that many degrees, on the menu that harmonic's own column carries

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
